title: China Tech Revolution Update — Jun 2, 2026
summary: China completed its bilateral tech war regulatory architecture on June 2 with two simultaneous moves. New 'Regulations on Trade Secret Protection' (effective June 2) formally classify AI training data, model weights, and algorithms as legally protected trade secrets for the first time under Chinese law — providing civil and criminal enforcement tools against data exfiltration from DeepSeek, Huawei, SMIC, and CATL IP. Simultaneously, a Chinese government-affiliated research team published a 63-sector counter-sanctions framework identifying technology domains (rare earths ~80%, solar ~90%, batteries, drones, AI architectures) where China holds sufficient global market share to impose export restrictions on the US and allies — mirroring US Entity List architecture. Together with the June 1 simultaneous bilateral tightening (China outbound investment regulation + US BIS global clarification), the decoupling now operates across seven formal vectors. BYD's May 28 in-house autonomous driving chip debut was also captured — joining Xpeng, Huawei MDC, and Horizon Robotics in China's domestic automotive AI silicon ecosystem.

title: China Tech Revolution Update — Jun 1, 2026
summary: China and the US enacted simultaneous bilateral technology control frameworks on June 1 in a historically notable policy symmetry. China's State Council published a 34-article outbound investment regulation (effective July 1) requiring approval for overseas tech, data, and personnel transfers — extending to HK, Macau, and Taiwan, granting retaliatory powers against discriminatory foreign entities, and completing Beijing's three-vector domestic containment architecture (capital in blocked, talent out travel-restricted, technology out reviewed). On the same day, US BIS clarified chip export restrictions apply to all Chinese-parented firms globally regardless of subsidiary location, closing a loophole exploited after the Trump administration reversed Biden's AI Diffusion Framework. The Wire China's May 31 analysis identified China's next AI challenge: compute cost pressure as agentic AI workflows replace chatbots, forcing Alibaba, Tencent, and Zhipu to raise prices while DeepSeek holds at $0.003625/M input tokens.
